The arrow keeps its true length. Its tip predicts the comparison point; the gap between them is the linearization error.

The variational equation is linear along a chosen solution. For nonlinear systems it is a first-order approximation, most accurate for small initial displacements over short times.

Explore nearby solutions

The base trajectory solves x′ = f(x). A comparison solves the same equation from a different initial point y₀. The variational vector solves η′ = Df(x(t))η, starting from η(0) = y₀ − x₀.

  • Follow the orange arrow. Its tail stays on the moving base point. At t = 0 its tip is exactly the comparison initial point. Later, the tip x(t) + η(t) is the linearized prediction, which need not lie on the actual comparison trajectory.
  • Choose an example. Linear flows make the prediction exact up to numerical error. Pendulum, Van der Pol, and Duffing examples show nonlinear effects. Explore Lorenz and Rössler flows in 3D to see sensitive dependence.
